title: Duchy of Normandy
capsule: The Duchy of Normandy originated in 911 when the Carolingian king Charles the Simple granted the lower Seine valley to the Viking chieftain Rollo by the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, in exchange for baptism, homage, and defence of the Frankish realm. Under Rollo's successors the duchy expanded westward to absorb the Contentin and Avranches by 933, and under Duke William the Bastard it became the springboard for the conquest of England in 1066. The duchy passed to the Plantagenet sphere under Henry II but was recovered by Philip II of France in 1204 after the fall of Château Gaillard, terminating Norman autonomy on the continent while the English crown retained the Channel Islands.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's boundaries after c. 1000 are well-documented through Frankish and Norman charters; the early tenth-century extent under Rollo is reconstructed from later sources and carries more uncertainty.
